response: ["Surgical excision with histologically negative margins is the recommended and first‑line treatment for primary cutaneous melanoma of any thickness, as well as for melanoma in situ.","Surgical margins should be based on tumor thickness.","Sentinel lymph node biopsy, when indicated, should be performed before wide excision of the primary tumor, and in the same operative setting whenever possible.","When melanoma is suspected, the whole lesion should be completely excised with a narrow (1–3 mm) margin to perform histological diagnosis.","Incisional biopsies can be performed on large lesions such as lesions on the face (e.g., lentigo maligna), acral lesions, and on the genitalia.","The consensus rate for this recommendation is 100 % (21/21).","The criteria driving the 7‑point score are: blue‑whitish veil (present, 2 points) and pigmentation (diffuse irregular, 1 point).","Blue‑whitish veil is defined as confluent blue pigment with an overlying white haze.","Diffuse irregular pigmentation is defined as asymmetric blotches of pigment.","The other criteria (pigment_network, vascular_structures, streaks, dots_and_globules, regression_structures) were scored as absent or typical and contributed 0 points.","The presence of a blue‑whitish veil and diffuse irregular pigmentation on the image contributes to the elevated score.","Visual verification of blue‑whitish veil and diffuse irregular pigmentation should be performed on the image."]
